central_question: What will be the state of the Iran conflict and nuclear standoff as of 31 December 2027 (renewed large-scale strikes, low-intensity conflict, durable ceasefire, negotiated framework, or regime crisis), and what are the probability-weighted implications for end-2027 and 2027-average Brent, gold, gas, macro and regional markets?

situation_brief.current_situation: A US-Iran war of attrition: Khamenei was killed in the February 28, 2026 opening strikes and succeeded by his son Mojtaba Khamenei in March; a June 2026 Memorandum of Understanding collapsed and formally expired in August. The US naval blockade, renewed July 13, 2026, has effectively halted Iranian crude exports (loadings 210 kbd mid-September; October reported at zero). The IAEA has had no access to declared enrichment sites since January 2026. Iran's economy faces a projected 7.7% contraction in fiscal 2026-27.
situation_brief.context: Two prior strike rounds damaged all three enrichment plants; surviving 60% uranium estimates range from 'a bit more than 200 kg' (Grossi) to 265-287 kg in Isfahan tunnels (ISIS). Talks via Qatari mediators are deadlocked: Iran offers to reopen Hormuz within seven days under its control for a blockade lift, eased export limits and released assets. The US and Israel reportedly have specific plans for a 'short but intensive operation' after the November 3, 2026 midterms. Brent averaged 102.0181 $/b (IMF) in September 2026; gold 4334.7467 $/oz; US CPI 3.717%; Fed funds midpoint 3.875%; ECB deposit rate 2.5%.
situation_brief.dynamics: Managed attrition dominates: the blockade severs Iran's revenue while Gulf exports recover above pre-war levels; OPEC-8 effective spare capacity is nearly exhausted (0.04 mb/d) and observed inventories are 509 million barrels below pre-war. Escalation pressure comes from collapsed IAEA verification, Iran's September 2026 preemption doctrine, pre-delegated missile authority, and Netanyahu's stated aim of overthrowing the regime. Restraint pressure comes from US war unpopularity (62% say the war was not worth it), the November 3 midterms, and Trump's repeated cancellation of major-combat plans.

scenarios.name: Low-intensity conflict
scenarios.narrative: The blockade, sabotage, cyber and proxy attacks continue without renewed state-on-state strikes, holding Iran suppressed but unresolved; prior: managed-standoff continuation dominates comparable post-strike episodes.

scenarios.name: Renewed large-scale strikes
scenarios.narrative: Iran's centrifuge reconstruction or breakout progress crosses Israeli or US red lines and re-strikes on nuclear or regime targets trigger Iranian retaliation; shifted up from a single-digit base rate by verified 2025-2026 strike precedent and collapsed IAEA access.

scenarios.name: Durable ceasefire
scenarios.narrative: Economic exhaustion and blockade attrition push Tehran to accept a durable ceasefire with verification but no nuclear diplomacy, freezing the conflict below the strike threshold.

scenarios.name: Negotiated framework
scenarios.narrative: US or Chinese-mediated talks convert the ceasefire into a partial nuclear framework with limited sanctions relief and restored IAEA access; requires a signed text, so weighted modestly absent current talks.

scenarios.name: Regime crisis
scenarios.narrative: Economic collapse under the blockade triggers succession upheaval or internal regime crisis that reshapes the conflict; single-digit weight as a tail absent a visible challenger coalition.

base_rates.reference_class: Named post-war ceasefires (2006 Lebanon; 2015 Yemen; Oct 2025 Gaza; Mar 2026 and Jun 2026 Lebanon), renewed large-scale state-on-state fighting within 2 years
